transcription_conventions: Anchors preserve source wording, with long s rendered as s and line-break hyphenation joined where unambiguous. Unicode planetary, zodiacal and aspect symbols represent visually decoded printed glyphs, rather than reproducing their original type shapes. Empty anchors indicate that a confident consecutive textual quotation was unavailable.
historical_scope: All statements below report the printed author's historical rules, conjectures or testimony. They do not identify actual thieves, establish gender or names, prove wrongdoing, or establish recovery by astrology.

units.short_original_anchor: respecting the Signe and quarter wherein they be
units.normalized_historical_statement: The opening continuation attributes women to ☿, ♀ and ☽, and men to ♄, ♃, ♂ and ☉, while requiring regard to the sign and quarter occupied.

This is the author's gender conjecture.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: If one Thiefe or more.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed subsection introducing methods for conjecturing one thief or several.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: it signifies to be one and no more
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author signifies one thief when the thief's significator is in a fixed sign and of direct ascensions, or in a sign of few children, or of few shapes and likenesses.
preconditions: Thief's significator in a fixed sign and of direct ascensions; alternatively, in a sign of few children or few shapes and likenesses.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The final two alternatives retain the source's compressed grammar.
A later immovable-sign rule on this page gives a competing plural result.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: a common or bycorporeall Signe
units.normalized_historical_statement: A two-bodied sign, identified here as common or bycorporeal, signifies more than one thief; the author calls that more likely when many peregrine planets are in that sign.
preconditions: Thief's significator in a two-bodied/common/bycorporeal sign.
Additional likelihood when many peregrine planets occupy that sign.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The peregrine-planets condition increases the stated likelihood rather than replacing the basic condition.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: it signifies more then one
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author signifies more than one thief when ☉ and ☽ behold each other by □ in the angles.
preconditions: ☉ and ☽ in the angles.
Mutual square aspect □.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No application or separation direction is specified.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: Signes that signifie many Children
units.normalized_historical_statement: The source's sign classifications are: many children—♋, ♏, ♓; few children—♈, ♉, ♎, ♐, ♑, ♒; diverse shapes or forms—♊, ♋, ♐, ♒; barren—♊, ♌, ♍; direct ascensions—♋, ♌, ♍, ♎, ♏, ♐; oblique ascensions—♑, ♒, ♓, ♈, ♉, ♊.
preconditions: Apply these printed classifications where the surrounding number-of-thieves rules invoke them.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The lists overlap; they have not been reconciled or replaced with modern classifications.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: be in the Angle of the Earth
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author conjectures more than one thief if ☽ at the hour of the question is in the Angle of the Earth in a common sign.
preconditions: ☽ at the question's hour.
Placement in the Angle of the Earth.
Common sign.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: there is but one Thiefe
units.normalized_historical_statement: The contrasting lunar rule conjectures only one thief if ☽ is in any of the other angles in a fixed sign.
preconditions: ☽ in an angle other than the Angle of the Earth.
Fixed sign.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The lunar subject carries forward from the preceding clause.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: Looke how many Planets are with the Thieves significator
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author assigns as many thieves as there are planets with the thief's significator.
preconditions: Count the planets with the thief's significator.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The word with is not given an orb or further technical definition here.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: in a common Signe more then one
units.normalized_historical_statement: A separate abbreviated rule attributes more than one thief to ☽ in a common sign.
preconditions: ☽ in a common sign.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This clause does not repeat the earlier angular qualification.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: that person is the principall actor
units.normalized_historical_statement: With the ascendant's lord in a male sign and the hour's lord in a female sign, the author conjectures a man and woman. He then selects as principal actor the person corresponding to the significator with which ☽ agrees, explicitly glossed as the one to whom she applies.
preconditions: Lord of ascendant in a male sign.
Lord of hour in a female sign.
Determine to whom ☽ applies.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The phrase as aforesaid refers outside this local clause.
Application, rather than separation, is explicit.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: the Angles moveable especially the first and seventh
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author conjectures more than one thief if the angles are movable, especially the first and seventh, or if the significator is in ♋, ♏ or ♓.
preconditions: Movable angles, with special emphasis on first and seventh; alternatively, significator in ♋, ♏ or ♓.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source gives these as alternatives; no aspect direction is specified.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: if it be immoveable, or a double bodied Sign
units.normalized_historical_statement: The source also says that an immovable sign or a double-bodied sign containing the thief's significator signifies more than one.
preconditions: Thief's significator in an immovable sign or a double-bodied sign.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed immoveable result competes with the earlier fixed-sign single-thief rule. It has not been silently corrected.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: Both the Luminaries beholding one another from Angles
units.normalized_historical_statement: Both luminaries beholding each other from angles are said to signify more than one thief.
preconditions: Both luminaries angular.
They behold one another.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This later clause specifies neither a square nor application/separation, unlike the earlier square rule.

units.section_heading: If one Thiefe or more.
units.short_original_anchor: doth demonstrate there were more Thieves then one
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author attributes more than one thief to ☽ in the ascendant when that is a double-bodied sign.
preconditions: ☽ in ascendant.
Double-bodied sign.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed subsection on conjectured clothing colours.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: You must know the colour of the Cloathing by the Planets
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author directs that clothing colour be judged from planets, signs, degrees and the house occupied by the significator, mixing those indications together. The sentence completes on p340 with colour of their Cloathes.
preconditions: Planets, signs and degrees.
House occupied by significator.
Mixture of the indications.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: These are historical colour conjectures, not observed clothing descriptions.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: If there be signification of many Theeves
units.normalized_historical_statement: Where many thieves are signified, the author directs judgment through the lord of the triplicity occupied by the significators.
preconditions: Signification of many thieves.
Identify the triplicity containing the significators and its lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No day/night triplicity distinction is supplied in this clause.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: The Significators of the Colours of the Planets after Alcabitius are these
units.normalized_historical_statement: Attributed to Alcabitius: ♄ gives black; ♃ green, spotted or ashy, or such like; ♂ red; ☉ tawny or saffron. For ☉, Lilly adds his own preference for a high sandy colour.
preconditions: Use the stated planet as colour significator.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The single-planet list here does not supply separate ♀, ☿ or ☽ colours.
Lilly's high sandy colour is explicitly his alternative conception.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: The Colors by mixing the Planets one with another are these
units.normalized_historical_statement: The printed ♄ mixtures are: with ♃, dark green or deep spotted with black; with ♂, dark tawny; with ☉, black-yellow and shining; with ♀, white-gray; with ☿, black or bluish; with ☽, deep tawny, deep gray or russet.
preconditions: Mix ♄ with the indicated second planet.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not make these mixtures depend on an explicitly stated conjunction or aspect.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: a Tawney, somewhat light spotted
units.normalized_historical_statement: The remaining ♃ mixtures are: with ♂, tawny, somewhat light spotted; with ☉, much like the Sun-and-Mars mixture but more shining; with ♀, greenish-gray; with ☿, spotted-green; with ☽, somewhat light green.
preconditions: Mix ♃ with the indicated second planet.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The ♃–☉ entry explicitly refers to the ☉–♂ mixture stated later.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: a light Red or Crimson
units.normalized_historical_statement: The printed ♂ mixtures are: with ☉, deep red shining; with ♀, light red or crimson; with ☿, red or red tawny; with ☽, tawny or light red.
preconditions: Mix ♂ with the indicated second planet.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No further Venus–Mercury–Moon pairings are supplied in this list.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: You must mix the colour of the Signifier
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author directs mixing the signifier's colour with the colour of its house to conjecture the clothes, or alternatively judging by the signs and degrees occupied by the signifier.
preconditions: Colour of signifier and colour of occupied house; alternatively, occupied signs and degrees.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The alternative method is retained separately from the planetary colour tables.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: as if he be in the Signe or House or Terme
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the signifier occupies ♄'s sign, house or term, the author instructs judgment according to ♄ as previously described.
preconditions: Signifier in the sign, house or term of ♄.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Sign, house and term are printed alternatives.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: judge after the mixture
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the signifier is in ♄'s house and ♃'s term, the author directs judgment by the ♄–♃ mixture, extending that procedure to the other planets.
preconditions: Signifier in ♄'s house.
Signifier in ♃'s term.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The extension to all others is general; additional mixture entries are not supplied here.

units.section_heading: Of the Cloathes of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: I have known it hold true very many times
units.normalized_historical_statement: In the printed left margin, Lilly says people conversant in judging many thefts might greatly perfect this judgment; he claims it has held true very many times, while saying his greater employments prevent further observations.
preconditions: Comment concerns the clothing-colour judgment beside which it is printed.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is the author's personal testimony and a limitation on his further observations.

units.section_heading: For Names.
units.short_original_anchor: For Names.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed subsection on conjectured names.

units.section_heading: For Names.
units.short_original_anchor: in Angles signifie short Names and of few Syllables
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author attributes short names with few syllables to ♃, ☉ and ♂ in angles; when near the Mid-heaven, he says they begin with A or E.
preconditions: ♃, ☉ or ♂ in angles.
Additional near-Mid-heaven condition for initial A or E.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Near is not quantified.
These are name conjectures.

units.section_heading: For Names.
units.short_original_anchor: the Name is of more Syllables
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author attributes a name of more syllables, exemplified by Richard or William, to ♄ or a second insufficiently resolved planetary glyph acting as significator.
preconditions: ♄ or the unresolved second printed glyph is significator.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The second glyph is not confidently decoded and has not been supplied from memory.

units.section_heading: For Names.
units.short_original_anchor: if the Querents Names be short
units.normalized_historical_statement: For the most part, the author says that if the querent's name is short, the quested person's name is also short.
preconditions: Querent's name short.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The qualification for the most part limits the assertion.

units.section_heading: Names of Theeves or Men, as Astrologers write.
units.short_original_anchor: Names of Theeves or Men, as Astrologers write.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed heading attributes the following name method to what astrologers write.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The heading is attribution, not evidence identifying any person's name.

units.section_heading: Names of Theeves or Men, as Astrologers write.
units.short_original_anchor: To know the Names by the Lord of the seventh House
units.normalized_historical_statement: The table is introduced as a method using the lord of the seventh house, a planet in the seventh house, or a planet joined with them.
preconditions: Seventh-house lord; alternatively, a planet in the seventh or a planet joined with them.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: These alternatives are retained without choosing one.

units.section_heading: Mens names.
units.short_original_anchor: Mens names.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed heading of the men's conjectured-name table.

units.section_heading: Mens names.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Columns are the principal significator and the planet joined. In row order, the conjectured mappings are: ☿/♂—Matthew; ☽/♀—Simon; ☉/♃—Laurence; ☿/☉—Clement; ☿/♄—Edmund; ♃/☉—John; ♄/♀—William; ♂/☉—Robert; ♂/☉—Peter; ♂/blank—Anthony; ☉/☿—Benjamin; ♃/♄—Thomas; ☉/blank—Roger; ☉/blank—Phillip; ♄/☉—George; ☉/♄—Andrew; ☽/☉—Henry; ☽/♄—Nicholas; ♃/☉—Richard; ☉/blank—James; ☉/blank—Stephen.

Duplicate planetary combinations produce different printed names.
No continuous 5–18-word prose anchor is available for this glyph table.
Names are authorial/table conjectures.

units.section_heading: Wo mens Names.
units.short_original_anchor: Wo mens Names.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed heading of the women's conjectured-name table, with a visible space within Womens.

units.section_heading: Wo mens Names.
units.normalized_historical_statement: The three glyph columns carry the labels The Significator, The Planets, and conjoyned. In row order, their conjectured mappings are: ♂/☿/blank—Katherine; ☿/♂/☉—Christian; ♄/☽/♀—Joane; ♀/♄/blank—Isabel; ♄/☉/blank—Elizabeth; ♄/☉/blank—Julian; ☽/♂/☉—Mary; ☽/♀/blank—Ellin; ♀/☿/blank—Agnes; ☉/☿/blank—Margaret; ☉/♀/blank—Alice; ☉/☿/blank—Edith; ☉/♀/blank—Maud; ☉/♃/blank—Lucy; ☉/blank/blank—Anne; ♃/blank/blank—Rachel; ☽/blank/blank—Nell, Ell-nor.
preconditions: Read all three printed glyph columns, retaining their row alignment.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Blank cells remain blank.
The table's duplicate combinations and third-column planets are retained.
No continuous 5–18-word prose anchor is available for this glyph table.
Names and gender categories are historical conjectures.

units.section_heading: Names of Theeves or Men, as Astrologers write.
units.short_original_anchor: Some moderne Professors have endeavoured to give a probable conjecture
units.normalized_historical_statement: The unheaded prose reports modern professors' attempts at probable conjecture of the Christian name of a thief or other person inquired after, man or woman. They first consider whether the principal significator is angular, then whether it aspects any planet or planets; the source explicitly says the aspect may be good or ill.
preconditions: Principal significator of the person inquired after.
Consider angularity.
Consider aspects to other planets, regardless of whether good or ill.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The text gives no separate angular/nonangular outcome here.
No application/separation requirement is stated.
The method is expressly a probable conjecture.

units.section_heading: Names of Theeves or Men, as Astrologers write.
units.short_original_anchor: if he be in no aspect
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the principal significator is in no aspect, these professors instead consider whose dignities it occupies and make their mixture from that.
preconditions: Principal significator in no aspect.
Determine whose dignities contain it.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The dignity types are not individually specified in this clause.

units.section_heading: Names of Theeves or Men, as Astrologers write.
units.short_original_anchor: for example; let us admit
units.normalized_historical_statement: Lilly supposes ☿ to be lord of the seventh and significator of a maid's lover, with ☿ in aspect to ♂ or in ♂'s dignities. Consulting the first table row, ☿ with ♂ gives Matthew; he would conjecture Matthew or a name equivalent in length or number of letters.
preconditions: ☿ lord of seventh and significator of a maid's lover.
☿ in aspect to ♂ or in ♂'s dignities.
Consult first row of preceding men's table.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is a hypothetical example rather than a worked chart or documented identification.
Equivalent length or letter count is an explicit alternative to the exact name.
No aspect type or direction is specified.

units.section_heading: Names of Theeves or Men, as Astrologers write.
units.short_original_anchor: for my part I never use this way
units.normalized_historical_statement: Lilly says he never uses this naming method and has not much credited it. Nevertheless, he believes that if well practised it might yield attractive conclusions and approach the very name or something near it.
preconditions: Assessment concerns the preceding table-based name method.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Explicit nonuse and limited credit.
Potential success is conditional on good practice and stated as belief, including approximation rather than certainty.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thief be of the house or not.
units.short_original_anchor: Whether the Thief be of the house or not.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed subsection on conjectured household membership.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thief be of the house or not.
units.short_original_anchor: If both the Lights behold the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author conjectures one of the family if both lights behold the ascendant or are in their own houses.
preconditions: Both lights behold ascendant; alternatively, both in their own houses.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No particular aspect or application/separation is specified.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thief be of the house or not.
units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the seventh in the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: The lord of the seventh in the ascendant gives the same family-member conjecture, through the source's idem.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Idem refers to the preceding family-member result.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thief be of the house or not.
units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the sixt in the second
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author conjectures a servant if the lord of the sixth is in the second.
preconditions: Lord of sixth in second house.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thief be of the house or not.
units.short_original_anchor: if either of the Luminaries behold the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: If either luminary beholds the ascendant, the author says the person is no stranger.
preconditions: Either luminary beholds ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This requires either luminary rather than both.
No aspect type or direction is specified.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thief be of the house or not.
units.short_original_anchor: it is an overthwart Neighbour
units.normalized_historical_statement: With ☉ opposite the ascendant, the author conjectures an overthwart neighbour.
preconditions: ☉ opposite ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The word overthwart is retained rather than expanded into an unstated character assessment.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thief be of the house or not.
units.short_original_anchor: beholding the ascendant with a friendly aspect
units.normalized_historical_statement: The lord of the seventh beholding the ascendant with a friendly aspect gives the same overthwart-neighbour result through idem.
preconditions: Lord of seventh beholds ascendant.
Friendly aspect.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not name the friendly aspect or its direction.
The apparent tension between friendly aspect and overthwart neighbour is preserved.

units.section_heading: A Stranger or Familiar.
units.short_original_anchor: A Stranger or Familiar.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed subsection offering further stranger/familiar conjectures.

units.section_heading: A Stranger or Familiar.
units.short_original_anchor: it is one of the house
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author conjectures someone of the house, or someone who frequents it, from ☉ and ☽ beholding the ascendant; alternatively, from the ascendant's lord in the first or joined to the seventh's lord.
preconditions: ☉ and ☽ behold ascendant; alternatively, lord of ascendant in first house or joined to lord of seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The sentence's compressed coordination is preserved.
No aspect direction is stated for beholding.

units.section_heading: A Stranger or Familiar.
units.short_original_anchor: the Luminaries in their proper houses
units.normalized_historical_statement: The luminaries in their proper houses, or in the house of the ascendant's lord, give the same house-member or frequent-visitor conjecture.
preconditions: Luminaries in their proper houses; alternatively, in the house of lord of ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The same refers to the preceding household/frequent-visitor result.

units.section_heading: A Stranger or Familiar.
units.short_original_anchor: in the Triplicity of the Lord of the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: In the continued luminary sequence, placement in the triplicity of the ascendant's lord is assigned a neighbour.
preconditions: The continuing luminary subject occupies the triplicity of lord of ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The subject is carried forward rather than restated in this abbreviated clause.

units.section_heading: A Stranger or Familiar.
units.short_original_anchor: in the Terms of him, a Familiar
units.normalized_historical_statement: In the same abbreviated sequence, placement in the ascendant lord's terms is assigned a familiar.
preconditions: Continuing subject in the terms of lord of ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source omits an explicitly repeated subject.

units.section_heading: A Stranger or Familiar.
units.short_original_anchor: brings back the Thief; without fail if they be Retrograde
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author says ☽ in the ninth in ⚹, □ or ☍ to ♄ or ♂ brings back the thief, adding without fail if they are retrograde.
preconditions: ☽ in ninth house.
Sextile ⚹, square □ or opposition ☍ to ♄ or ♂.
Additional retrograde condition for the emphatic without fail claim.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The plural pronoun they is not explicitly resolved; it appears to refer to the named planets.
No applying or separating direction is printed.
The return claim remains historical testimony.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: Another.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed unnumbered heading introduces another collection of relationship conjectures.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: and not the ascendant, the Thief is knowne to the owner
units.normalized_historical_statement: The author conjectures that the thief is known to the owner when ☉ and ☽ aspect the ascendant's lord but do not aspect the ascendant.
preconditions: ☉ and ☽ aspect lord of ascendant.
They do not aspect the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Negative ascendant condition is explicit.
No particular aspect or direction is specified.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: the Significator of the Thiefe strong in the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: The thief's significator strong in the ascendant is said to denote a brother or kinsman.
preconditions: Thief's significator strong.
Placement in ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Strong is not further defined here.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: Lord of the seventh in the ninth from his owne house
units.normalized_historical_statement: In a clause introduced by Zael, the seventh's lord in the ninth from his own house is said to signify a stranger.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in ninth counted from his own house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The turned-house reference is retained; it is not replaced with the radical ninth.
The source attribution is Zael.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: beholding each other, a Kinsman
units.normalized_historical_statement: ☉ and ☽ beholding each other are assigned a kinsman.
preconditions: ☉ and ☽ behold one another.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No angularity, particular aspect or direction is specified in this relationship rule.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the ascendant in the third or fourth
units.normalized_historical_statement: The ascendant's lord in the third or fourth is said to accuse the querent's own household servant.
preconditions: Lord of ascendant in third or fourth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Accuseth is the source's historical claim, not an accusation established by this outline.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: this I have oft proved true by experience
units.normalized_historical_statement: Lilly claims he has often proved the immediately preceding household-servant rule true by experience.
preconditions: Immediately follows the lord-of-ascendant-in-third-or-fourth rule.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Personal author testimony; no individual case or chart is supplied.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed subsection arranging relationship conjectures by the seventh lord's house placement.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the ascendant or fourth
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh's lord in the ascendant or fourth is said to denote someone of the house or household, or a frequent visitor; someone in the city or town whom the querent least mistrusts and who will hardly confess the fact.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in ascendant or fourth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: All relationship, location, suspicion and confession qualifiers are source assertions, not findings about an actual person.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: noteth one of the houshold, or an acquaintance
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh's lord in the second, if in a masculine sign, is said to denote someone of the household or an acquaintance.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in second house.
Masculine sign.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The masculine-sign parenthesis qualifies this branch of the printed rule.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: if it be in a feminine Signe
units.normalized_historical_statement: For the seventh's lord in the second in a feminine sign, the author conjectures the querent's wife, perhaps a sweetheart or maid of the house. He adds that it is within the power of the loser or someone of his house and may be recovered by money.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in second house.
Feminine sign.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Perhaps qualifies the sweetheart/maid alternatives.
The pronoun it shifts or compresses the reference between person and lost thing; that ambiguity is retained.
Recovery by money is only the source's claim.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the third
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh's lord in the third is assigned someone of the kindred: brother, sisters, cousins; or the querent's onely Fellow by way of service; or a neighbour often in his sight; or his disciple, messenger or servant, etc.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in third house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The unusual printed wording onely Fellow is retained without substituting another relationship.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the fourth
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh's lord in the fourth is assigned the querent's father, an old person, someone of the father's kin, or someone dwelling in the father's heritage or house. The author adds that the thief has given it to his wife, or a woman to her husband; alternatively it is the goodman or goodwife of the house, or a tiller or the incompletely printed Labou- of the land for the querent.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in fourth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The series combines conjectured identities and a conjectured transfer of the thing; both are retained.
The occupational word after Tiller is incomplete in the visible printing and is not silently completed.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: the Sonne or Daughter of him
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh's lord in the fifth is assigned the querent's son or daughter, or the son or daughter of his cousin or nephew, with the parenthesis if the Sign be a masculine; alternatively someone of his father's household or his very friend.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in fifth house.
Retain the masculine-sign parenthesis beside the cousin/nephew alternative.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The exact breadth of the parenthetical masculine-sign qualification is grammatically uncertain; its placement is preserved rather than generalized.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the sixt
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh's lord in the sixth is assigned a servant, disciple or labourer to the querent; someone conversant with a churchman; a brother or sister of the father; a sick person; an unsteadfast person; or a grieved person.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in sixth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The bodily and personal descriptions are the author's conjectures, not clinical or character findings.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the seventh
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh's lord in the seventh is assigned the querent's wife or lady, a harlot, a woman usually suspected for such matters, or a buyer or seller in markets.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in seventh house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: These labels report historical conjectures and prejudicial terminology; they establish no identity or wrongdoing.
The adjacent printed caution is preserved in C070.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: This must be warily understood.
units.normalized_historical_statement: A printed marginal caution beside the seventh-house paragraph says this must be understood warily.
preconditions: Applies locally to the adjoining seventh-house relationship claims.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not explain the caution further or restrict it to one expressly named alternative.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: the Taker is an utter enemy to the Loser
units.normalized_historical_statement: Within the seventh-in-seventh paragraph, the author says that if it is a feminine sign, the taker is an utter enemy of the loser because of some former cause between them, lives somewhat far from him, still holds the things in custody, and they are hard to recover.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in seventh house.
Feminine sign.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is retained alongside, rather than reconciled with, the paragraph's wife/lady alternatives.
The custody and recovery claims are historical assertions.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the eighth, a Stranger
units.normalized_historical_statement: The visible beginning assigns a stranger to the seventh's lord in the eighth, followed by the unfinished qualification yet seem-. The catchword eth indicates continuation beyond this window.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in eighth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The qualification and remainder are unavailable here. No completion from memory or an unprovided page has been supplied.

units.section_heading: ERRATA.
units.short_original_anchor: ERRATA.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Supplementary printed heading introducing the original correction list.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The errata image has no visible printed page number.

units.section_heading: [Unheaded preface above ERRATA.]
units.short_original_anchor: the Printers are unacquainted with this kind of learning
units.normalized_historical_statement: The introductory note asks readers not to wonder at material faults, explaining that such things are seldom printed locally and printers are unfamiliar with this learning. The author supposes there may be some faults but very few, says the most observable literal faults are listed, and asks readers to correct them.
preconditions: Reader encounters material or literal printing faults.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author says I suppose and does not claim that every fault is listed.
Inspection of the complete correction list found no entry for printed p339–343; no correction has been imported from another page.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The early rule combines a fixed sign and direct ascensions with one thief, while the later clause explicitly gives more than one for an immoveable sign or double-bodied sign.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: Opposing source methods must remain separate. The supplied errata lists no correction for this page.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The second glyph after ♄ in the more-syllables naming rule is insufficiently clear for confident decoding.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: One alternative significator in C029 remains unresolved; it has not been filled from remembered editions.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: Several name-table rows repeat the same planetary combination with different names, and some joined-planet cells are blank.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: Duplicates and blanks are source data, not mistakes to normalize into a unique identification.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The triplicity and terms clauses omit a repeated subject. The nearby retrograde clause uses the plural pronoun they.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: The continued luminary subject and probable planetary referent are marked as contextual readings, not explicit restatements.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The friendly-aspect rule ends in idem immediately after the overthwart-neighbour result.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: The printed referral is preserved without replacing it with a more congenial result.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: In the fourth-house rule the occupational word following Tiller is visibly incomplete at the line end, with of the Land beginning the next line.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: C066 retains the incomplete occupational word instead of silently restoring a guessed suffix.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The fifth-house masculine-sign parenthesis follows the cousin/nephew alternative, leaving its full grammatical scope uncertain.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: The qualification is retained at its source position rather than imposed on every alternative.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The seventh-house paragraph gives wife/lady and other relationship alternatives, then a feminine-sign enemy clause, with a marginal warning to understand it warily.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: The competing descriptions and caution are retained separately rather than reconciled.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: The eighth-house rule ends with yet seem- and catchword eth.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: Only the visible stranger attribution is available; the missing qualification must be recovered from the next original page in a later authorized window.

unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.issue: No errata entry targets printed p339–343.
unresolved_glyphs_or_source_conflicts.importance: The supplied correction list supplies no authority to alter this window's competing wording or uncertain glyph.
